text.p: Leading Venezuelan paper company Venepal has capitalised some 28 billion bolivars ($59.5 million) of last year's retained earnings in a reward to its shareholders, Venepal said.
"We wanted to distribute those profits to our shareholders," Executive Vice President Jorge Nissensohn told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.

Each shareholder, of both A and B shares, will receive two new shares following Thursday's extraordinary general meeting. The 28.23 billion bolivar share dividend will increase total paid-up capital to 42.35 billion bolivars.
The meeting also agreed to increase the company's authorised capital to 60 billion bolivars.
"Some nine billion of that will be put towards our global depositary share program (GDS)," Nissensohn said. "The remainder we'll leave as slack should we want to pay out dividends later this year."

Nissensohn said the current ratio of three B shares per each GDS will be adjusted to nine shares, "as a reflection of the devaluation of the bolivar. We simply want each GDS to reflect a more significant bolivar value".
The meeting also agreed to maintain open lines of credit worth eight billion bolivars.
In September, Venepal reported nine month net profits of 12.714 billion bolivars versus 4.23 billion bolivars, all in constant July 1996 bolivars.
